# rm safety hook — design intent (packs/general/deletions.py)

Shipped in 9.19.0 (commit 8e32bb48, 2026-07-16) after two adversarial codex passes. macOS **trash rewrite** added in 9.29.0 (ae212caf). **Rebuilt on the `visit=` primitive + blast-radius denies + nested-shell descent** in general pack 0.27.0 (repo 10.1.0, 2026-07-18) — see [[rm-trash-rewrite-shipped]].

## Threat model

An **accident guard, not a security boundary.** It lexically analyzes the pre-execution Bash command; a determined evader always wins (see the removed read-only approver: static lexical proof is unsound). The asymmetry that makes a blocker sound where the approver wasn't: a **blocker fails safe** — a missed spelling is just the pre-hook status quo, while a false block costs one agent roundtrip and the deny message says what to do instead. Everywhere below "fail open" means "miss it (accident-guard status quo)", "fail closed" means "deny".

## Structure (0.27.0)

Registration is `rewrite_command_occurrences(visit=visit_rm, only_if=[Command(r"(?i)\brm\b")])` — the primitive contributes `Tool("Bash")` and walks occurrences, threading a `WalkContext(cwd, plain_words, spliceable)`. `visit_rm` dispatches on the (normalized) executable: `rm` → `handle_rm`; a shell/eval program whose `nested_command_string` payload is non-None → `descend_rm`. Pack policy (`handle_rm`, `check_rm_target`, `blast_radius_block`, glob machinery, `Recoverable`/`Trashed`, `trash_binary`, `GLOB_LIMIT`) stays in deletions.py. **Shared utils extracted:** `captain_hook/util/vcs.py` owns `in_vcs_repo`/`is_repo_root`/`scanned_names`/`contains_repo`; `captain_hook/util/shell.py` owns `emit_token` (was `emit_target`) + `SAFE_WORD`/`plain_words`, `resolve_cd`, and the promoted `nested_command_string`/`safe_parse_command_line`/`SHELL_C_FLAG`/`NESTED_COMMAND_DEPTH` (the fixes-pack danger classifier re-imports these — a change to the shared helper moves both).

## Rules and thresholds

- **(a) Outside-repo block/rewrite**: any literal target (or glob *match*) with no `.git`/`.jj` marker in itself or an ancestor. `.git` may be a FILE (worktrees/submodules) — the check is `.exists()`, never `.is_dir()`. On macOS with a resolvable `trash`, a recoverable outside-repo target is **rewritten** to `<trash> <targets>` instead of denied; elsewhere (or when emission forfeits) it denies. Exemption: `captain_hook/util/scratch.is_scratch_path` — the **shared seam** with `packs/fixes/scratch_writes.py`; never fork a second scratch definition.
- **(b) Blast-radius hard-denies** (`blast_radius_block`, macOS rewrite path only, gated on `rewritable = trash is not None`): the target `resolved` is `os.path.normpath`-normalized (so a trailing `..` can't dodge equality), then matched in order — tier 1 `== Path("/")` ("filesystem root"), tier 2 `== Path.home()` or `Path("/Users") in (home, home.parent)` ("home directory"), tier 3 `is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) and contains_repo(dir)` ("contains git/jj repositories"). **Order is load-bearing** (cheap equality before the scan). Gated on `rewritable` so non-macOS / non-spliceable paths keep byte-identical pre-tier behavior at zero scan cost. `contains_repo` is a bounded **unpruned** `os.walk` (followlinks=False) that fails **closed** at 20,000 entries (inlined literal, mirrors the glob budget). This tier fires only in the outside-vcs branch — a target *inside* an outer repo is still allowed (git recoverability); a nested repo under a tracked dir is a known pre-existing gap (expanding it would false-deny on vendored `.git` dirs).
- **(c) Glob limit**: `GLOB_LIMIT = 10`. Counting is bounded (islice / budgeted walk). **Deliberately NOT scratch-exempt.** Globs matching >10 files and too-broad globs **deny on every platform** — a deliberate post-review narrowing (rewriting them trashes a repo root hiding beyond the `limit+1` collection prefix); don't restore the oversized-glob rewrite without exhaustive match verification.
- **(d) Repo-root block**: a literal target that is itself a repo root — deleting it destroys the history rule (a)'s recoverability rests on. Denied on every platform.
- **Walk budget**: `**` patterns walk at most 20,000 entries (inlined in `recursive_glob_matches`; os.walk followlinks=False — symlink loops miscount under iglob). Exhaustion **fails closed**. Tested by monkeypatching the `walked_paths` seam with synthetic paths.

## Two walk seams — never merge

`walked_paths` (glob matching) **prunes** dot-entries, so it can never see `.git`. `scanned_names` (contains_repo) is **unpruned** precisely so it can. Distinct functions in distinct modules; merging one into the other silently breaks either glob dot-handling or repo detection.

## Symlink policy

The leaf is **never dereferenced**: `rm` unlinks the entry, not the referent, so `resolve_target` resolves the parent and preserves the final component, and tier-3 uses `is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)`. A symlink leaf pointing at a catastrophic dir therefore trash-rewrites (removing the link) rather than hard-denying — accepted (recoverable).

## cwd and token semantics

- cwd threads through the primitive walk (`WalkContext.cwd`, seeded from `evt.cwd`) and, independently, inside `descend_rm` payloads. `resolve_cd` returns the target only when it **is an existing directory**; a `cd` to a nonexistent path leaves the shell at the prior cwd (a failed `cd` doesn't move), and a dynamic/`-`/multi-arg `cd` returns None (relative targets then skip — fail-open). A **piped** `cd` (`occurrence.piped`) is not threaded (its cwd change doesn't persist). **Known gap:** a subshell `(cd X)` parses identically to a bare `cd X` in cc-transcript 14.0 (parens stripped, `.piped` False) so it still threads wrongly — upstream, backlogged.
- **Nested-shell descent** (`descend_rm`, check-only): `sh`/`bash -c` payloads and `eval` args are re-parsed (`safe_parse_command_line`, RecursionError → None) and rm-checked, depth-capped at `NESTED_COMMAND_DEPTH = 3`. A nested risky rm **denies** (never rewrites inside a quoted payload; it passes `trash=None`). Depth exhaustion and unparseable payloads **fail open** (accident guard — do not harden). `SHELL_C_FLAG = re.compile(r"-[a-z]*c")` matches combined clusters (`-lc`, `-xc`, …), not just `-c`.
- `$`-containing **rm targets** evaluate as literal paths (fail-closed). Tokens/executables get dequoting + backslash unescaping + casefolded basename — local normalization that duplicates what cc-transcript should own; delete when upstream task d026e9cd lands.

## Deliberate punts — do not "fix" locally

- **Wrapper option arity** (`env -u HOME rm`, `sudo -u root bash -c rm`, `timeout 5s rm`): `Command.unwrapped` limitation, upstream task d026e9cd. (Plain `sudo`/`env`/`command`/`nohup bash -c` DO descend and deny — unwrapped strips the bare wrapper.)
- **Subshell `(cd X)` cwd leak**: upstream parser gap (occurrence loses subshell membership).
- **Brace expansion, quoted globs/tilde, string-concat (`"rm"" -rf /"`), case-insensitive APFS aliases (`/users/yasyf`), eval-cd side effects, `xargs rm`/`find -delete`/`$(...)`**: adversarial-shaped, not accident-shaped, or dropped by the parser entirely.

## Testing landmines

- pytest `tmp_path` is **scratch-exempt through TWO independent branches** (macOS `/var/folders` TEMP_ROOT; Linux `/tmp` name-ancestor) — both neutralized by the shared `no_scratch` fixture in `tests/test_pack_deletions.py`. Reproduce Linux topology with `TMPDIR=/tmp uv run pytest tests/test_pack_deletions.py`.
- Blast-radius tests patch `captain_hook._packs.general.deletions.trash_binary` (force present) and `Path.home` (never the runner's real `~` — dotfiles flip outcomes); the zero-scan case patches `contains_repo` to a `pytest.fail` sentinel. `contains_repo` unit tests patch `captain_hook.util.vcs.scanned_names`. Post-extraction, patch symbols at their **new home** — a `monkeypatch.setattr` on a moved name in the deletions namespace patches a dead alias.
- `in_vcs_repo` negative tests must not assume `tmp_path` lacks a VCS-marked ancestor (basetemp inside a checkout breaks it) — assert on `is_repo_root` (dir-only, deterministic) + a marker-present positive instead.
- Inline `tests=` run on the real filesystem — only **machine-independent** cases (`cwd="/"` absolutes: `rm -rf /`, `bash -lc 'rm -rf /'`) belong there; fixture-dependent cases live in `tests/test_pack_deletions.py`. Use `printf`/files, not `echo`, for escaped spellings.
